issues.t: Oil leak from timing cover seal on V6
issues.sym: Oil seeping or dripping from the front or side of the engine, oil smell, or oil spots under the car.
issues.why: On early twin-turbo V6 Macans the timing case cover seal can leak, possibly because of unsuitable bolts. Fixing it means dropping the engine, which was originally rated as about a 40-hour job.
issues.next: Have a specialist confirm where the oil is coming from. Ask for records of earlier repair work if you are buying. Independent shops now have quicker workarounds than the factory method.

issues.t: Transfer case vibration or jerking at low speed
issues.sym: Shudder, vibration or jerking when pulling away slowly, worse with the steering turned, such as in parking lots.
issues.why: The transfer case that sends power to the front wheels can develop faults. In the US Porsche extended the warranty on it to seven years with unlimited miles and reimbursed owners who had already paid.
issues.next: Have a Porsche dealer check the transfer case and ask whether the extended warranty still covers your car.

issues.t: Cracked fuel pump flange can leak fuel (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell or fuel wetness near the rear seat area or under the car.
issues.why: The fuel pump cover can rub against the fuel flange, which may crack and leak fuel, raising fire risk.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, have the car checked right away. A dealer will rework or replace the flange for free.

issues.t: Brake booster damaged during assembly (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels harder than normal and the car takes more effort to stop.
issues.why: On Macans built from March to April 2014, the brake booster may have been damaged when it was installed, reducing brake assist.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect and replace the booster for free.

issues.t: Rear seat belt anchor screw not tightened (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no sign. A loose anchor may move when you pull on the belt.
issues.why: The screw holding the lower seat belt anchor to the rear outboard seat frames may not have been tightened properly, so the anchor could come loose in a crash.
issues.next: Have a dealer replace and tighten the screws for free.

issues.t: Loose shock absorber screws (recall)
issues.sym: Clunks, unstable handling, or a car that pulls or wanders.
issues.why: The screws holding the front and rear shock absorbers may not have been tightened properly, which can damage the brakes and cause loss of control.
issues.next: Do not drive the car until a dealer has tightened the connections. It's free.

issues.t: Water pump leak causing low boost
issues.sym: Coolant loss, a check engine light, and the engine feeling down on power.
issues.why: On the 2.9 twin-turbo V6, a failing water pump can leak coolant into the vacuum lines. That upsets the turbo wastegate controls and limits boost.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure-tested and the vacuum lines checked. Replace the pump before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Turbocharger oil supply line leak
issues.sym: Oil smell, smoke from the engine bay, or oil residue around the turbos.
issues.why: The oil feed lines to the turbochargers on the early V6 can leak.
issues.next: Have the turbo oil lines inspected. Leaking oil near hot turbos is a fire risk, so do not ignore it.

issues.t: Vacuum leak from crankcase ventilation (PCV)
issues.sym: Check engine light with lean or vacuum leak codes, rough idle, or a whistle.
issues.why: On early V6 engines, vacuum leaks usually trace back to the crankcase ventilation (PCV) system.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the PCV parts smoke-tested for leaks.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption on V6
issues.sym: Needing to add oil often, such as a pint every 500 miles, sometimes with blue smoke.
issues.why: Some V6 engines burn oil, which PistonHeads says may point to piston ring problems.
issues.next: Keep a log of oil added and have a specialist run an oil consumption test and check for leaks.

issues.t: Misfire from failed ignition coil or worn spark plugs
issues.sym: Flashing or steady check engine light, rough idle, and shaking under acceleration.
issues.why: Ignition coils fail and spark plugs wear, especially on the turbocharged engines.
issues.next: Have the codes read and replace the failed coil. Replace plugs on schedule.

issues.t: Driveshaft center bearing clunk and vibration
issues.sym: A clunk when pulling away or shifting, and vibration felt through the floor.
issues.why: The center support bearing or the rubber coupling on the driveshaft to the front axle wears out.
issues.next: Have the driveshaft and bearing inspected. Aftermarket bearings are often seen as the better long-term fix.

issues.t: Air suspension sagging or compressor running constantly
issues.sym: One corner or end sits lower, a suspension warning, or the compressor running a lot.
issues.why: Leaks in an air spring, shock or hose, a faulty valve block, a bad connection or a ride height sensor can upset the air suspension. A compressor that never runs may only need a relay.
issues.next: Have the system scanned and leak-tested before replacing the compressor. Driving with a sagging corner can wear out the compressor.

issues.t: PDK shudder or jerky shifts at low speed
issues.sym: Shuddering or jerking in lower gears and reverse, or clunky low-speed shifts.
issues.why: The PDK dual-clutch gearbox can have clutch control problems, and owners of later cars also report shudder in low gears.
issues.next: Have the dealer check for software updates and confirm the PDK fluid has been changed on schedule.

issues.t: Infotainment (PCM) freezing or restarting
issues.sym: The center screen freezes, reboots, shuts off, shows the wrong language or won't load maps.
issues.why: Software and hardware faults in the Porsche Communication Management (PCM) unit.
issues.next: Try a system reset and ask the dealer for software updates. If the hardware has failed, specialists can repair units for less than a new one.

issues.t: ABS and stability warning lights from wheel speed sensor
issues.sym: ABS and PSM (stability control) warning lights come on.
issues.why: A faulty wheel speed sensor is a common cause.
issues.next: Have the codes read to find which sensor is at fault. The brakes still work normally but without ABS.

issues.t: Exhaust chirp after revving
issues.sym: A chirping noise after revving to about 2,000 rpm and lifting off the throttle.
issues.why: On early cars the exhaust mounts and brackets could chirp. Later cars got new downpipes and brackets.
issues.next: Not harmful. A dealer or specialist can fit the updated brackets.

issues.t: Sunroof leaking into the cabin
issues.sym: Water on the headliner, seats or floor after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: The sunroof drains clog with dirt and leaves, so water overflows into the cabin. Owners brought a class-action suit that Porsche settled.
issues.next: Have the sunroof drains cleared and keep them clean at each service.

issues.t: Air conditioning not cooling well
issues.sym: Weak cooling or the climate system stopping completely.
issues.why: Owners report A/C faults on newer Macans, ranging from poor cooling to complete failure.
issues.next: Have the A/C pressures and codes checked while it is still under warranty.

issues.t: Peeling trim and dash rattles
issues.sym: Trim peeling or cracking on the B-pillars and center console, and rattles from the dash and doors.
issues.why: Owners report trim finish and fit problems on newer Macans.
issues.next: Report it to the dealer under warranty and have loose trim padded or re-clipped.

issues.t: Rearview camera blurry or blank on Macan Electric (recall)
issues.sym: The reverse camera image is blurry or doesn't appear.
issues.why: A fault with the camera or its control software means the image may not show, so the car doesn't meet the federal rear visibility rule.
issues.next: Have a dealer update the software and replace the camera if needed. It's free.

issues.t: Headlights too bright for US rules on Macan Electric (recall)
issues.sym: Oncoming drivers flash their lights at you.
issues.why: The headlight software was set to European instead of US standards, so the beams can glare at other drivers.
issues.next: Have a dealer reprogram the headlight software. It can't be done over the air, and it's free.

issues.t: Front seat airbag not fastened correctly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning sign.
issues.why: On a few Macan 4 Electrics, the front seat airbag screw was driven into the frame instead of through the airbag housing, so the airbag may not deploy properly.
issues.next: Have a dealer check and correct the airbag screw connection for free.
